title: Shop Missing Leads in DMs - AI Sorts Hot Leads You Approve
content:
Your shop or agency is missing leads in the DMs.
Someone asks for a price, you reply 3
hours later, and they are already gone.
I built a flow that SORTS hot leads and
DRAFTS the reply.
You just approve.
This is the Wednesday business reel in my
build-in-public week.
Yesterday I showed a lead-qualification
agent for form leads.
Today is the Instagram DM version for
shops and agencies.
Stay till the end, because the human
approval step is the whole product.
Here is the problem in plain English.
Your Instagram inbox mixes buyers, spam,
job seekers, and friends.
If you answer everything in order, hot
buyers wait.
If you rush every reply, you sound pushy or wrong.
You need a sorter before you need a faster typer.
Step 1. Write hot, warm and cold rules in
PLAIN ENGLISH.
Hot might mean: asked for price, named a
service, and left a phone number.
Warm might mean: asked what you offer, but
no timeline.
Cold might mean: "hi", a collab pitch, or
a student project request.
If you cannot write the rules, the AI
cannot follow them.
Step 2. The automation SCORES the thread
and DRAFTS a reply.
It does not send.
Imagine a boutique agency gets 25 DMs a day.
Say 5 look like real buyers, 8 are vague,
and the rest are noise.
The agent tags each one, writes a short
reason, and drafts a reply in a note.
A human still presses send.
Step 3. Put a HUMAN APPROVAL GATE before
any outbound message.
This is the same pattern businesses use
with workflow tools for irreversible
steps.
Your DM agent can read and draft.
It CANNOT INVENT A DISCOUNT, a delivery
date, or a promise you did not write down.
You approve. Then it sends. Or you edit.
Or you kill it.
Step 4. Log every decision for a weekly review.
Score, reason, draft, and whether you
approved or changed it.
After 1 week you will see which rules are
too loose.
After 2 weeks you tighten the hot definition.
That is how the system gets better without
going unsupervised.
Imagine you are in a client meeting and a
hot DM arrives.
The agent drafts: thanks for asking about
X, here is the next step, want a 15-minute
call?
You glance, tap approve, and keep the meeting.
That is the payoff. Speed with judgment,
not speed without it.
Here's my take.
DM automation that auto-sends is a brand risk.
DM automation that sorts and drafts is a
sales tool.
Start with score plus draft. Keep the
human on the send button.

agency, DM me.
Comment 'AI' on Instagram and I'll send
you the free checklist, or grab the link
in the LinkedIn post.
Follow for your daily AI update.
